You must not pervert justice or show favoritism. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of those who are in the right.
Pursue justice, nothing but justice, so that you may live and take possession of the land that Yahweh your God is giving you.
“Do not plant any kind of tree as an Asherah pole next to the altar you build for Yahweh your God,
and do not set up for yourself a sacred stone, which Yahweh your God hates.

notes.text: Hebrew “the month of Abib” (“ear of grain”), the month when the barley ripened, later called Nisan. It is the first month of the year counted from spring (Exodus 12:2; 13:4). The Hebrew calendar is lunar, so the modern equivalent is approximate.
Hebrew “in the evening, at the going down of the sun.” Exodus 12:6 has the Passover lamb slaughtered “between the two evenings,” that is, at twilight.
Hebrew Shavuot, later also called Pentecost, held seven weeks after Passover, in the third month, Sivan (May–June).
Or “Tabernacles” (Hebrew Sukkot), held in the seventh month, Tishri (September–October); see Leviticus 23:34.

verses.text: “You must not sacrifice to Yahweh your God an ox or a sheep that has a blemish or any defect at all, for that is detestable to Yahweh your God.
“Suppose there is found among you, in one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you, a man or woman who does what is evil in the sight of Yahweh your God by breaking his covenant,
and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven, which I have forbidden,
and it is reported to you and you hear of it. Then you shall make a thorough inquiry, and if it is true and the fact is confirmed that this detestable act has been done in Israel,
you shall lead out to your town gates the man or the woman guilty of this wicked deed, and that man or woman shall be stoned until dead.
On the testimony of two or three witnesses the one who is to die shall be put to death. No one shall be put to death on the word of a single witness.
The hands of the witnesses shall be the first raised against him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.

“If a case arises in your towns that is too difficult for you to decide—between one kind of bloodshed and another, one legal claim and another, or one kind of injury and another, any matter of dispute—then rise up and go to the place Yahweh your God chooses.
Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who holds office in those days. Consult them, and they will declare to you the verdict.
Then you must act according to the decision they announce to you from that place that Yahweh chooses. Be careful to do exactly as they instruct you.
Act according to the instruction they teach you and the ruling they give you. Do not depart from the sentence they pronounce, either to the right or to the left.
Anyone who acts arrogantly and will not listen to the priest who stands there to minister before Yahweh your God, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall burn away the evil from Israel.
All the people will hear of it and be afraid, and they will not act presumptuously again.
“When you come into the land Yahweh your God is giving you and have made it yours and are living there, and you say, ‘Let me put a king over myself, like all the surrounding nations,’
you may indeed set over yourself a king whom Yahweh your God chooses. Set as king over you one from among your own brothers; you may not put a foreigner over you, one who is not your brother.
Only he must not acquire great numbers of horses for himself, or send the people back to Egypt to get more horses, since Yahweh has told you, ‘You shall never go back that way again.’
He must not take many wives for himself, or his heart will turn away, and he must not pile up for himself great amounts of silver and gold.
Once he is seated on his royal throne, he is to copy out for himself on a scroll this law,{a} from the text in the keeping of the Levitical priests.
It shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Yahweh his God by keeping all the words of this law and these statutes and doing them,

so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers, and so that he may not stray from the command, to the right or to the left. Then he and his sons will reign long over his kingdom in the midst of Israel.

notes.text: The Septuagint renders “a copy of this law” as to deuteronomion touto, “this repetition of the law” (Brenton), literally “this second law,” from which the book’s English name, Deuteronomy, comes.

verses.text: “The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, shall have no share or inheritance with Israel. They shall live on the food offerings{a} made to Yahweh, which are his inheritance.
They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; Yahweh himself is their inheritance, as he promised them.
This shall be the priests’ due from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
You shall also give him the firstfruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first fleece of your sheep.
For Yahweh your God has chosen him and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of Yahweh for all time.
“If a Levite comes from one of your towns anywhere in Israel where he has been living, and he comes with all the desire of his heart to the place Yahweh chooses,
then he may minister in the name of Yahweh his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before Yahweh.
He shall receive an equal portion to eat, besides what he receives from the sale of his family’s possessions.{b}
“When you enter the land Yahweh your God is giving you, do not learn to copy the detestable practices of those nations.
Let no one be found among you who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, or who practices divination, or tells fortunes, or reads omens, or is a sorcerer,
or casts spells, or consults ghosts or familiar spirits, or seeks answers from the dead.
Whoever does such things is detestable to Yahweh, and it is because of these detestable things that Yahweh your God is driving those nations out before you.
You must be blameless before Yahweh your God.
These nations whom you are about to dispossess listen to fortune-tellers and diviners, but as for you, Yahweh your God has not allowed you to do so.
“From your own midst, from among your brothers, Yahweh your God will raise up a prophet like me for you. To him you shall listen.
This is what you asked of Yahweh your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, ‘Let us not hear the voice of Yahweh our God again or see this great fire any more, or we will die.’
And Yahweh said to me, ‘They have spoken well.
From among their brothers I will raise up a prophet for them, one like you. My words I will place in his mouth, and he will speak to them all that I command him.
Whoever will not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will call him to account.
But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that same prophet shall die.’
And if you say in your heart, ‘How can we tell which word Yahweh has not spoken?’—
when a prophet speaks in the name of Yahweh and the thing does not happen or come true, that is a word Yahweh has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.

notes.text: Hebrew ’isshe, offerings presented by fire or as food gifts; the exact sense is debated.
Hebrew obscure; literally “besides his sales according to the fathers.”

verses.text: “When Yahweh your God has cut off the nations whose land he is giving you, and you have driven them out and are living in their cities and houses,
you shall set apart three towns for yourselves in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to possess.
Prepare the roads, and divide into three parts the territory of the land that Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills a person may flee there.
This is the rule for the one who kills someone and flees there to save his life: he must have struck his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in the past.

For example, a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and as he swings the axe to fell a tree, the head flies off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies. That man may flee to one of these towns and live.

Otherwise the avenger of blood,{a} in hot anger, might pursue the killer and overtake him because the way is long, and strike him dead, though he did not deserve death, since he had not hated his neighbor in the past.
That is why I command you to set apart three towns for yourselves.
And if Yahweh your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your forefathers, and gives you all the land he promised to give to your forefathers—
provided you take care to keep all this command that I give you today, loving Yahweh your God and walking always in his ways—then you shall add three more towns to these three,
so that innocent blood may not be shed in the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, and so that bloodguilt may not be on you.
“But if a man hates his neighbor and lies in wait for him, attacks him, and strikes him a fatal blow so that he dies, and then flees to one of these towns,
the elders of his own town shall send for him, have him brought back from there, and deliver him into the hand of the blood avenger, and he shall die.
Show him no pity. You must purge the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
“Do not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you will receive in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to possess.
“A single witness shall not be enough to convict a person of any crime or offense that he may have committed. A matter shall be established only on the evidence of two witnesses or of three.
If a malicious witness rises up against someone to accuse him of wrongdoing,
then both parties to the dispute shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges who are in office in those days.
The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness turns out to be a false witness who has testified falsely against his brother,
then you shall do to him what he had intended to do to his brother. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
Those who remain will hear and fear, and no one will ever again commit such wickedness among you.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

notes.text: Hebrew go’el haddam, the relative responsible for avenging a kinsman’s death.

verses.text: “When you march out to battle against your enemies and you see horses and chariots, a people more numerous than you, do not fear them, for Yahweh your God is with you, he who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
As you approach the battle, the priest is to step forward and address the troops.
He shall say to them, ‘Hear, Israel: today you are drawing near to battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not tremble before them,
for Yahweh your God is the one who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.’
Then the officers shall speak to the people, saying, ‘Has anyone built a new house and not yet dedicated it? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
Has anyone planted a vineyard and not yet enjoyed its fruit? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man enjoy its fruit.
Has anyone become engaged to a woman and not yet married her? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man marry her.’
Then the officers shall say further to the people, ‘Is any man fearful and faint of heart? He should return home, lest his fellow soldiers lose courage as he has.’
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, commanders of the troops shall be appointed to lead them.
“When you draw near to a town to fight against it, first offer it terms of peace.
If it answers you peaceably and opens its gates to you, then all the people found in it shall serve you at forced labor.
But if it will not make peace with you but makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.
And when Yahweh your God gives it into your hand, you shall strike down all its males with the edge of the sword.

But the women, the children, the animals, and whatever else is in the town, all its plunder, you may seize for yourselves, and you may make use of what you take from your enemies, which Yahweh your God has given you.
That is the way to deal with all the cities far away from you, those that do not belong to the nations nearby.
But in the towns of these peoples that Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
You must devote them to complete destruction—the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite{a}—as Yahweh your God has commanded you,
so that they will not teach you to do all the detestable things they have done for their gods, and so cause you to sin against Yahweh your God.

“When you lay siege to a city for many days, fighting against it to take it, do not ruin its trees by putting an axe to them. Eat their fruit, but do not chop them down. Is the tree of the field a man, that it should come under siege from you?{b}
Only the trees you know do not bear fruit you may destroy and cut down, to build siegeworks against the town that is making war with you, until it falls.

notes.text: The Septuagint adds “and the Girgashite” (the Samaritan Pentateuch is reported to agree), making seven nations as in 7:1.
Or “for the tree of the field is man’s life.” The Hebrew is difficult.

verses.text: “Suppose a murdered body is discovered lying in a field in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to possess, and no one knows who struck him down.
Your elders and judges shall go out and measure from the body to each of the towns around it.
Then the elders of whichever town is closest to the body shall take a young cow that has never been put to work or drawn a load under a yoke.
The elders of that town shall bring the heifer down to a valley with running water, which has never been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they shall break the heifer’s neck.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for Yahweh your God has chosen them to serve him and to give blessings in Yahweh’s name, and every lawsuit and case of violence is to be decided by what they say.
All the elders of that town nearest the slain man shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,
and they shall declare, ‘Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it done.
Make atonement, Yahweh, for your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, and do not lay the guilt of innocent blood on your people Israel.’ Then the bloodguilt will be atoned for on their behalf.
In this way you will remove from among you the guilt of innocent blood, by doing what is upright in Yahweh’s eyes.
“When you march out to fight your enemies, and Yahweh your God hands them over to you and you carry off prisoners,
and you see among the captives a beautiful woman and desire her and take her as your wife,
then you shall bring her home to your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails.

She shall take off the clothes she was wearing when captured and stay in your house, mourning her father and her mother for a full month. After that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
But if you are no longer pleased with her, you shall let her go wherever she wishes. You must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have humbled her.
“Suppose a man has two wives, one whom he loves and one whom he does not, and each of them has borne him sons, but the eldest son was born to the wife who is not loved.

then on the day he divides his property among his sons as their inheritance, he may not treat the son of the loved wife as firstborn in place of the son of the unloved wife, who is the true firstborn.

Instead, he must acknowledge as firstborn the son of the unloved wife by giving him a double portion of all that he has, for that son is the firstfruits of his strength; the right of the firstborn is his.
“If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or his mother, and though they discipline him, he will not listen to them,
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his town at the gate of his place.
They shall tell the elders of the town, ‘Our son here is defiant and disobedient; he refuses to listen to us. He eats too much and drinks too much.’
Then all the men of his town shall stone him until he dies. In this way you will remove the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear of it and fear.
“If a man has committed a crime worthy of death and is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his body must not remain all night on the tree. You must bury him that same day, for anyone hanged is under God’s curse.{a} You must not defile the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.

notes.text: Or “an insult to God.” Galatians 3:13 quotes this verse in a form close to the Septuagint.

verses.text: “If you see your brother’s ox or his sheep straying, do not pretend you have not seen them. Be sure to bring them back to your brother.
If your brother does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take the animal home with you and keep it until he comes looking for it; then give it back to him.
Do the same with his donkey, with his cloak, and with anything your brother loses and you find. You must not look the other way.
If you see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not turn away from them. You must help him lift them up again.
“A woman shall not wear a man’s gear, and a man shall not put on a woman’s garment, for whoever does such things is detestable to Yahweh your God.
“If you happen upon a bird’s nest along the road, in a tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs and the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, do not take the mother along with the young.
Let the mother go free, though you may take the young for yourself, so that things may go well with you and you may live long.
“When you build a new house, put a parapet around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if anyone falls from it.
“Do not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeited,{a} both the crop you sowed and the fruit of the vineyard.
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
Do not wear cloth woven of wool and linen mixed together.
“Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap around yourself.
“Suppose a man marries a woman and goes in to her, and then turns against her,
and charges her with shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, ‘I married this woman, but when I came near her I found no proof of her virginity.’
Then the young woman’s father and mother shall bring out the proof of her virginity to the elders of the town at the gate.
Her father shall say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he has turned against her.

Now he has accused her of shameful things, claiming, “Your daughter was not a virgin when I found her.” Yet here is the evidence that she was.’ Then they are to unfold the garment in front of the town’s elders.
The elders of the town are then to seize the man and discipline him.

They shall fine him 2½ pounds of silver{b} and give it to the young woman’s father, because he has given a bad name to a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife; he may never divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the accusation proves true, and the evidence that the girl was a virgin cannot be found,

then they shall bring her out to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her town shall stone her to death, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting as a prostitute in her father’s house. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
“If a man is found lying with a woman who is married to another man, both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman as well as the woman. So you shall burn away the evil from Israel.
“If there is a young woman who is a virgin, pledged to be married to a man, and another man meets her in the town and lies with her,

bring the two of them out to that town’s gate and stone them until they die—the girl because, though she was inside the town, she raised no cry, and the man because he dishonored the wife of his neighbor. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
But if it is out in the countryside that the man meets the engaged young woman, and he seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
Do nothing to the girl, for there is no sin in her that deserves death. It is just as when a man rises against his neighbor and kills him.
For he met her in the open country, and though the engaged young woman cried out, there was no one to rescue her.
“If a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and not pledged to be married, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
the man who lay with her shall give the young woman’s father 20 ounces of silver,{c} and she shall become his wife, because he has humbled her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.
“A man shall not take his father’s wife, and so uncover the edge of his father’s garment.{d}

notes.text: Hebrew “become holy,” that is, forfeited to the sanctuary.
Hebrew “a hundred of silver,” that is, 100 shekels, about 40 ounces or 1.15 kilograms.
Hebrew “fifty of silver,” that is, 50 shekels, about 20 ounces or 575 grams.
Verse 30 is 23:1 in the Hebrew text. To “uncover the skirt” of the father is to violate his marriage; compare Ruth 3:9.

verses.text: “No man who has been castrated, whether by crushing or by cutting, may come into the assembly of Yahweh.{a}
No one born of a forbidden union{b} may come into the assembly of Yahweh; not even his offspring to the tenth generation may come into Yahweh’s assembly.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of Yahweh; even to the tenth generation none of them may ever enter the assembly of Yahweh,
because they did not come to meet you with food and water along the way after you left Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim{c} to curse you.
But Yahweh your God would not listen to Balaam; instead Yahweh your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because Yahweh your God loves you.
As long as you live, never work for their welfare or their good.
“Do not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
Their grandchildren, the third generation born to them, may come into Yahweh’s assembly.
“When you are encamped against your enemies, guard yourself from everything evil.
If any man among you is unclean because of something that happened to him at night, he must go outside the camp; he must not come back into the camp.
When evening comes he shall bathe in water, and at sunset he may come back into the camp.
Mark out a spot outside the camp to which you can go out for your needs.
Among your equipment you shall have a digging tool, and when you squat outside, dig a hole with it and turn back and cover your excrement.

For Yahweh your God walks about in the middle of your camp to rescue you and to give your enemies over to you. Therefore your camp must be holy, so that he will not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
“Do not hand back to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.
Let him live with you, among you, in whatever place he chooses within one of your towns, wherever suits him best. Do not oppress him.
“No Israelite woman is to become a shrine prostitute,{d} and no Israelite man is to become one.
You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute or the price of a dog{e} into the house of Yahweh your God to pay any vow, for both of them are detestable to Yahweh your God.
“Do not charge your brother interest, whether on money, food, or anything else that may be lent at interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that Yahweh your God may bless you in everything you put your hand to in the land you are entering to possess.
“When you make a vow to Yahweh your God, do not be slow to fulfill it, for Yahweh your God will certainly require it of you, and you would be guilty of sin.
But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Whatever has passed your lips you must be careful to carry out, just as you freely vowed to Yahweh your God with your own mouth.
“When you go into your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you like, until you are full, but you must not put any in your basket.
When you go into the grain field of your neighbor, you may pick ears by hand, but you must not swing a sickle at his standing grain.

notes.text: Verses 1–25 are numbered 2–26 in the Hebrew text.
Hebrew mamzer, a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps one born of incest or of a marriage forbidden by the law.
Aram-naharaim means “Aram of the two rivers,” the region of upper Mesopotamia.
Hebrew qedeshah (feminine) and qadesh (masculine), literally “consecrated one”; the exact practice referred to is debated.
“Dog” probably refers to a male prostitute.

verses.text: “Suppose a man marries a woman, and later she does not find favor in his eyes because he has found in her some matter of indecency, so he writes her a document of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house.
After leaving his house, she goes off and marries another man.
If the second husband also dislikes her, writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house, or if the second man who married her dies,

then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back to be his wife after she has been defiled, for that would be detestable before Yahweh. You must not bring guilt on the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.
“When a man has newly married, he shall not go out with the army or be assigned any public duty. He shall be free at home for one year to bring joy to the wife he has taken.
“No one shall take a pair of millstones, or even the upper millstone, as security for a debt, for that would be taking a person’s livelihood{a} as security.
“If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers from among the Israelites, and treats him as a slave or sells him, that kidnapper shall die. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
“In cases of a skin disease,{b} be very careful to do everything the Levitical priests instruct you. As I commanded them, so you shall take care to do.
Keep in mind how Yahweh your God dealt with Miriam along the road after you left Egypt.
“If you lend anything at all to your neighbor, you must not enter his house to fetch what he offers as a pledge.
Wait outside, and the one who is borrowing from you shall carry the pledge out to you.
And if he is a poor man, do not go to sleep with his pledge.
Be sure to return the pledge to him at sunset, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. It will be counted as righteousness for you before Yahweh your God.
“Do not exploit a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the foreigners who live in your land within your towns.
Give him his wages each day before the sun sets, for he is poor and is counting on it. Otherwise he may cry out against you to Yahweh, and you will be guilty of sin.
“Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children be put to death for their fathers. Each one shall be put to death for his own sin.
“Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s garment as security.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that Yahweh your God ransomed you from there. For this reason I am commanding you to do this.

“When you harvest the grain of your field and overlook a sheaf there, do not turn back for it. Leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, do not go over the branches a second time. What is left shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not glean it afterward. What is left shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.

notes.text: Hebrew “life” (nephesh).
Hebrew tsara‘at, traditionally “leprosy,” a term covering various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13–14.

verses.text: “When men have a quarrel and go to law, and the judges hear the case, they shall declare the innocent man in the right and the guilty man in the wrong.
If the one in the wrong deserves a flogging, the judge shall have him laid down and flogged in front of him, with as many lashes as his wrongdoing calls for.
Forty blows may be given him, but no more, or else, if he is beaten with more blows than these, your brother would be degraded in your sight.
“You shall not put a muzzle on the ox as it threshes.

“When brothers live together and one of them dies and has no son, the dead man’s wife shall not marry outside the family to a stranger. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother{a} to her.
The firstborn son she bears shall stand in the place of the dead brother and bear his name, so that his name is not erased from Israel.

But if the man does not wish to take his brother’s wife, then his brother’s wife shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, ‘My husband’s brother refuses to keep his brother’s name alive in Israel; he will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother to me.’
The elders of his town shall then call for him and talk with him. If he stands firm and says, ‘I have no desire to marry her,’

then his brother’s widow is to approach him while the elders watch, draw his sandal from his foot, and spit in his face. And she shall say, ‘So may it be done to the man who refuses to build up his brother’s household.’
And in Israel his family shall be called ‘The House of the Unsandaled.’
“When men are fighting with one another, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the man striking him, and she reaches out and seizes him by his private parts,
then you shall cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
“You shall not have in your bag two kinds of weights, a heavy and a light.
Do not keep two different measures in your house, one larger and one smaller.
You shall have a full and honest weight; you shall have a full and honest measure,{b} so that your days may be long in the land Yahweh your God is giving you.
For everyone who does such things, everyone who deals dishonestly, is detestable to Yahweh your God.
“Remember what Amalek did to you on the way as you came out of Egypt,
how he met you on the way when you were faint and weary and attacked all the stragglers at your rear. He did not fear God.

So when Yahweh your God gives you rest from all the enemies surrounding you in the land he is giving you to inherit and possess, you are to wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.

notes.text: Hebrew yabam, the levirate duty, from Latin levir, “husband’s brother.”
Hebrew “ephah,” a dry measure of about 3/5 bushel (22 liters), standing here for measures of capacity in general. Verse 14 likewise has “an ephah and an ephah,” that is, two different measures.

verses.text: “Once you have entered the land Yahweh your God is giving you to inherit, have taken possession of it, and are living there,

you shall take some of the first of all the produce of the ground that you harvest from your land that Yahweh your God is giving you. Put it in a basket and go to the place Yahweh your God chooses to make his name dwell.
Go to the priest who is in office in those days and say to him, ‘I declare today to Yahweh your God that I have come into the land Yahweh swore to our forefathers to give us.’
Then the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of Yahweh your God.

And you shall respond before Yahweh your God, ‘My father was a wandering Aramean.{a} He went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner, few in number, and there he became a great nation, mighty and numerous.
But the Egyptians mistreated us, oppressed us, and imposed harsh slavery on us.
Then we cried out to Yahweh, the God of our forefathers, and Yahweh heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
And Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and with wonders.
He led us into this place and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, look, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that you, Yahweh, have given me.’ Then set it down before Yahweh your God and bow down before Yahweh your God.
And you shall rejoice in all the good that Yahweh your God has given to you and to your household, you and the Levite and the foreigner who is among you.

“When you have finished paying all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of tithing, and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that they may eat within your towns and be satisfied,

then you shall say in the presence of Yahweh your God, ‘I have cleared out of my house the portion that is holy and have handed it over to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not broken or forgotten any of your commands.

I did not eat any of it while mourning, nor did I take any of it out while unclean, nor have I given any of it for the dead. I have listened to the voice of Yahweh my God and done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling place, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the ground you have given us, as you swore to our forefathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.’
“This day Yahweh your God commands you to do these statutes and rulings. Be careful to do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today you have declared that Yahweh is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commands, and his rulings, and obey his voice.
And Yahweh has declared today that you are a people belonging to him, his own treasure, just as he told you, and that you are to keep all his commands,
and that he will set you high above all the nations he has made, in praise, in fame, and in honor, and that you shall be a people holy to Yahweh your God, as he promised.”

notes.text: Or “a perishing Aramean” or “an Aramean about to perish,” probably referring to Jacob. The Septuagint reads “My father abandoned Syria.”
